Kṣemarāja's commentary: whose greatness is unmeasured, who measures the world from earth to Sadāśiva in the heart, who displays creation-dissolution plays — he alone, of non-dual nature, endowed with his own autonomy-power, established in his own nature, like an ocean unmoved by world-waves, shines supreme. paragraphs.text: There is exactly one winner: Shiva. He throbs with his own aliveness, stands on nothing but himself, and tastes everything from the inside.

He is the lord of the whole Kula, the whole family of all things. He himself cannot be measured, but he measures the entire world — from the earth under your feet all the way up — inside his own heart. He puts on creation and destruction the way a stage puts on plays, and he stays steady through all of it, the way the deep ocean stays steady while waves move on top.
And here is the part about you: recognizing means tasting that very same throb inside your own inward face. That tasting is the whole win.

paragraphs.text: One winner, ever: Shiva. Self-throbbing, self-standing, tasting everything from the inside out. No committee, no contest.

He is the lord of the entire Kula — the whole family of everything that is. Unmeasured himself, he measures the world end to end inside his own heart, runs creation and destruction like plays, and does not move while the world waves crash. Non-dual, self-powered, supreme.
And the punchline is you: recognition means tasting that exact same throb in your own inward face. That is it. That is the whole thing.
